To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the [3H]-DHA binding to intact lymphocytes isolated form rat spleen is rapid and readily reversed.
beta adrenoceptors of rat lymphocyte were labeled by [3H]dihydroalpreno1ol, and the beta adrenoceptor binding sites in rat lymphocyte could be divided into two classes.

[3H]dihydroalprenalol binds to beta-adrenoceptor in rat spleen lymphocytes with a KD of about 7 nmol.L- 1, Bmax of about 80 fmol/10 7 lymphocytes, and the affinity of the high-affinity site is about 3 orders magnitude higher than that for the low-affinity site.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an assay for beta-adrenoceptors using intact lymphocytes isolated form rat spleen.
the radioligand binding of [3H] DHA in lymphocytes.
the development of a simple and rapid method for the determination of the number of beta-adrenoceptors on intact rat lymphocytes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
[3H]DH A binding to lymphocytes isolated from the rat spleen is specific, saturable, and reversible.
the beta-adrenergic receptor in lymphocytes is a single class of sites with a KD of about 7 nmol.
beta-adrenoceptors are expressed on rat spleen lymphocytes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
[3H] DHA can be used to label beta 1-adrenoceptors in rat spleen lymphocytes.
beta-adrenoceptors are present on rat lymphocytes, and they have the same properties as those of beta-adrenoceptors present in other tissues.
beta-adrenoceptors on lymphocytes isolated from spleen of rats have a single high affinity site and a low affinity site.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the binding of [3H] DHA to intact lymphocytes isolated rat spleen is a useful and reliable method for measuring beta-adrenoceptors.
beta-adrenoceptors are expressed in rat splenic lymphocytes, and their number and affinity are different from those reported for beta-adrenoceptors from other tissues.
[3H] DHA is suitable for beta-adrenoceptor binding studies in intact lymphocytes and that the beta-adrenoceptors on lymphocytes can be divided into two classes of sites with different affinity.
